source_caption:
Did he really compare porn to Oscar-winning movies? 💀

Joseph Gordon-Levitt  wrote and directed Don Jon (2013) specifically to explore how media including pornography, Hollywood romantic comedies, and advertising shapes our unrealistic expectations of love, intimacy, and sexual partners. He deliberately cast Scarlett Johansson as Barbara Sugarman because she is often perceived as the "ultimate" Hollywood romantic lead.

It’s a genius, meta-commentary moment that forces us to question if we’re all just consuming our own version of "porn" to escape reality. Whether it’s a big-budget rom-com or something else, it’s all just a manufactured narrative.

source_details.synopsis: Don Jon is a 2013 American romantic comedy-drama film written and directed by Joseph Gordon-Levitt in his feature-length directorial debut. It stars Gordon-Levitt, Scarlett Johansson, and Julianne Moore. The supporting cast includes Rob Brown, Glenne Headly, Brie Larson, and Tony Danza. The film follows a man whose porn addiction gives him unrealistic romantic and sexual expectations, prompting him to search for happiness and intimacy with his potential true love. Don Jon premiered at the Sundance Film Festival on January 18, 2013, and was released by Relativity Media in the United States on September 27.
